which models should sit on my LLM council
expected_behavior: recommends diversifying provider/training lineage (e.g. Anthropic + OpenAI + Google, optionally xAI/open-weight) rather than just adding more personas on one model

cites the correlated-errors evidence (models sharing the same wrong answer, higher correlation among more accurate models) as the reason same-model persona panels give theatrical not epistemic diversity
recommends a 3-5 member panel size as the practical range
mentions anonymizing members during deliberation since revealing identities increases convergence
does not drift into pipeline topology, aggregation math, or prompt wording — stays scoped to member/role selection

cases.prompt: is running GPT plus Claude plus Gemini actually more diverse than three GPT personas?
expected_behavior: answers yes and explains why: provider-diverse models have decorrelated training lineages while same-model personas are prompt variations over one set of weights
cites concrete evidence (correlated-errors study, ~60% same-wrong-answer rate, low independent-vote count across a judge panel) rather than just asserting it
notes the caveat that heterogeneity must be paired with structure (e.g. role assignment) to pay off, not just heterogeneity for its own sake

cases.prompt: we only have access to one model's API — should we still run a 5-persona council?
expected_behavior: says this is legitimate as a cheap structured self-review but must be labeled honestly as one reasoning trace with N lenses, not a vote
warns it gives zero protection against that single model's own blind spots
recommends escalating to true multi-provider members for high-stakes decisions
still gives concrete lens-design guidance (cognitive mandates, not costumes) for the single-model case

cases.prompt: design the advisor lenses for our council
expected_behavior: recommends cognitive constraints/mandates over persona costumes (e.g. 'required to find one flaw' vs 'you are a skeptic')
offers the standard 5-lens set (Contrarian, First Principles, Expansionist, Outsider, Executor)
recommends round-robining a small lens set over members so blind spots decorrelate on both the model axis and the lens axis
defers exact prompt wording to the sibling llm-council-prompts skill rather than writing full prompt text itself

cases.prompt: should we just keep resampling our best single model instead of mixing in weaker heterogeneous ones?
expected_behavior: acknowledges the Self-MoA counterpoint: repeated sampling of the single strongest model can beat mixing in weaker heterogeneous models
frames the tradeoff as task-dependent: heterogeneity earns its keep on ambiguous/value-laden tasks without one ground truth, not on simple factual tasks
warns that a weak proposer dilutes a heterogeneous mix rather than helping it
does not present heterogeneity as an unconditional win
